# <b>Gasoline Dispensing
Operations</b>

General Permit
Help Sheet continued...

Maricopa County Air Quality Department logo: a green-and-blue circular wave motif, with the text “Maricopa County”, “AIR QUALITY”, and “DEPARTMENT”.

## Areas of Concern

## <b>Spill Containment Receptacles</b>

Keep your spill containment receptacle free from
debris and liquid. Be sure to check your spill
containments at least weekly or after each fuel
delivery.

## <b>Vapor Recovery Lines</b>

The driver/operator of a gasoline cargo tank must
ensure that vapor recovery equipment is properly
connected and in use at all times during loading.
The vapor valve shall be a poppetted dry break valve
that is CARB-certified and spring loaded.

## <b>Tank Integrity</b>

Fill pipe assembly must be intact and not loose.
Inspect weekly at minimum to ensure the threading is
maintained tightly.

## Remember to...

## <b>Pay the annual fee.</b>

An annual administrative fee is due every year on
the date of ATO issuance. To ensure you receive
your annual invoice, please update any changes to
your contact information by completing a Contact
Information Update Form online:
<u>maricopa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/5581</u>
Paying your annual fee does not renew your ATO.

## <b>Renew your ATO prior to the pre-set
expiration date.</b>

The Gasoline Dispensing Operations General Permit
expires on November 3, 2023 and every five years
thereafter, regardless of when your ATO was issued.
No renewal fee is required. The renewal application
can be found at:
<u>maricopa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7035</u>

A row of white horizontal gasoline storage tanks with piping, hazard placards, and yellow protective bollards.
